title: Checkpoint: The Americas
objective: After this level you can describe the main mountains, rivers and regions of North and South America.
summary: The Pan-American Highway runs Alaska to Argentina, broken only by the Darién Gap. The Continental Divide follows the western mountains, and big rivers drain the land east of them.

cards.headline: You can drive from Alaska to the tip of South America. Almost.
cards.body: One road network runs nearly 30,600 km down both continents, and there's exactly one place where it stops cold. Let's take the trip anyway, with everything from this chapter in the glovebox.

cards.headline: Follow the spine
cards.body: The Pan-American Highway runs from Alaska and Canada all the way to the southern tip of Argentina. For the whole trip, a mountain spine keeps you company: the Continental Divide, which runs from western Alaska along the Rockies, through Mexico and Central America, and down the Andes. Two continents, one long rooftop.

cards.fact: The only break is the Darién Gap: about 100 km of roadless rainforest.
cards.context: It lies between Panama and Colombia, exactly where Level 76's narrow isthmus joins North America to South America. So the one road built to link the two continents stops right at the seam between them.

mascot.line: All that road, and the missing piece is exactly where the continents meet. Classic.

cards.headline: Mountains west, rivers east
cards.body: Step back and both continents share a design. Tall mountains line the west, and giant rivers drain the land east of them. The Mississippi runs south to the Gulf of Mexico, fed by the Missouri from the Rockies. The Amazon flows east from the Andes to the Atlantic. Same blueprint, drawn twice.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 complete
learned: The Pan-American Highway runs Alaska to Argentina
Its only break is the Darién Gap, where the continents join
The Continental Divide follows the Rockies and the Andes
Mountains west, big rivers draining east, on both continents

questions.prompt: Where is the only break in the Pan-American Highway?

options.label: In the Canadian Rockies
options.rationale: The road runs through Canada without a break.

options.label: At the Mississippi delta
options.rationale: The highway's gap is in Central America's rainforest.

questions.explanation: The Darién Gap, about 100 km of roadless rainforest between Panama and Colombia, is the highway's only break.

questions.prompt: Why is the Darién Gap such an awkward place for the highway to break?

options.label: It sits in the middle of the Rockies
options.rationale: It's in the rainforest between Panama and Colombia.

options.label: It is right where the two continents join
It is the widest part of Central America
options.rationale: The isthmus narrows near Panama; it isn't wide there.

options.label: It is in the Caribbean islands
options.rationale: The gap is on the mainland.

questions.explanation: The isthmus links North and South America, and the Darién Gap sits exactly at that seam.

questions.prompt: From Levels 72 and 79: the Continental Divide runs along which two great ranges?

options.label: The Appalachians and the Andes
options.rationale: The Appalachians are in the east; the divide follows the western mountains.

options.label: The Rockies and the Sierra Madre Oriental
options.rationale: The divide follows the western mountains, not Mexico's eastern range.

options.label: The Great Plains and Patagonia
options.rationale: Those are flat lands, not ranges.

questions.explanation: The divide runs from Alaska along the Rockies, through Mexico and Central America, and down the Andes.

questions.prompt: From Level 73: which river carries water from the Rockies into the Mississippi?

options.label: The Ohio
options.rationale: The Ohio joins from the east.

options.label: The Colorado
options.rationale: The Colorado carved the Grand Canyon.

options.label: The St. Lawrence
options.rationale: The St. Lawrence drains the Great Lakes to the Atlantic.

questions.explanation: The Missouri begins in the Rockies of Montana and is the Mississippi's longest tributary.

questions.prompt: What design do North and South America share?

options.label: Flat land everywhere, no big ranges
Mountains only down the middle
options.rationale: The big ranges line the west.

questions.explanation: Both continents have tall western mountains, the Rockies and the Andes, with giant rivers, the Mississippi and the Amazon, draining the land to their east.
